name: context-compaction
context: Long-running agent conversations or tasks that exceed the context window limit. Compaction periodically summarizes the accumulated context — including user messages, assistant reasoning traces, tool calls, and tool results — into a high-fidelity summary, then replaces the full history with the summary. This enables the agent to continue working without losing essential information while staying within the context budget. Unlike scratchpad-note-taking (selective note-taking) or conversational-memory (windowing), compaction is a whole-context lossy compression that preserves key decisions and facts.
benefits: Enables arbitrarily long task completion within a fixed context window
Distills context to what matters — decisions, open questions, key facts
Agent continues with minimal performance degradation
Works for any agent without structural changes
tradeoffs: Compaction itself requires an LLM call (latency and cost)
Information loss is inevitable — overly aggressive compaction loses critical context
Must preserve enough detail to allow meaningful continuation
Tool call records become opaque after compaction (only tool_use record remains)
use_cases: Long coding sessions that exceed the context window
Research agents processing large document collections
Autonomous agents running multi-hour training sequences
Customer support agents handling long troubleshooting sessions
avoid_when: Tasks that fit entirely within the context window
Latency-sensitive applications where compaction overhead is prohibitive
Tasks where specific verbatim records must be preserved for compliance
anti_patterns: Compacting too aggressively and losing critical context
Never compacting and running into context overflow
Compacting without preserving open questions and pending decisions
design_principles: Compact when context reaches a token threshold (e.g., 95% of window)
Preserve: open questions, pending decisions, key facts, architectural choices
Discard: verbatim tool outputs, redundant reasoning traces, old user prompts
best_practices: Tune the compaction prompt for your domain — preserve what matters
Serialize the compaction block so the model knows context was summarized
Test compaction trajectories by querying for specific facts from before compaction
references: Anthropic, Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents: Compaction, 2025 — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents
